angleRead.text: The dossier gives me three seasons of Travis Coles and the rates I can work from them. The 2041 line is the one that stands out — 22-4, 2.72 ERA, 215 innings — but the rate that matters is the walk column: 39 walks against 254 strikeouts, a 6.51 K/BB. That is not a normal season for him. In 2040 he was at 3.39, in 2039 at 3.88. The 2041 number is nearly double his own two-year baseline. The question is whether that is a real change in how he throws or a single season of good fortune on balls in play and sequencing. plan.focus: Travis Coles's 2041 walk rate against his own two prior seasons and the 2041 peer band on the Athletics staff.
plan.why: The 6.51 K/BB in 2041 is the single largest rate change in the three-season dossier, and it is the load-bearing number under his 22-4 record. Without it, the ERA is not repeatable.
checks: Confirm the 2041 walk total (39) and strikeout total (254) against the innings figure (215) before publishing the 6.51 rate.
Verify the 2040 and 2039 rates from the season lines, not from memory.
Check that the peer rates for Dillon and Rivas are computed from their listed lines and not from any other source.

plan.interpretation: The 2041 season is the hinge. The two prior seasons show a competent starter with good but not elite command. The 2041 walk rate is a step change, and the peer band makes it look less like a staff-wide environment and more like something specific to Coles. But one season is variance until a second season confirms it.
